analysis.title: 2027: Great Expectations, but Risky Business (World Outlook)
key_insights: DB sees world growth of 3.5% in 2027 vs 3.3% in 2026, and global inflation easing from 3.9% to 3.7%. AI investment supports activity while energy, rates, fiscal and geopolitics offset.
Equity strategists treat last week's sell-off as a vol event that may extend but does not derail fundamentals. They target S&P 500 at 9,000 by end-2027 (about 25% above current) and Stoxx 600 at 750.

US growth is forecast at 2.3% annual in 2027 (2.4% in 2026). AI capex added about 0.9pp to annualised growth before one-third to one-half import leakage, and equipment spending growth is seen moderating from about 16% to about 10%.

DB expects the Fed to hike 75bp more, with 25bp moves in December, January and March, taking fed funds from 3.875% to 4.625%. Nominal neutral is put at 3.75-4%, and markets price a January hike with 70+% probability.
US inflation is sticky. Headline CPI averages 2.7% in 2027 vs 3.4% in 2026, and core PCE ends 2026 above 3% before easing to 2.5% by Q4 2027. Super core is at 3-4% and AI adds price pressure.
The breakeven monthly payroll number is estimated at about 25-50k, so small payroll gains are consistent with a stable labour market. Unemployment is forecast at 4.1-4.2% in 2027.
Euro area growth is forecast at 1.2% in 2027, with HICP at 3.1%. The ECB deposit rate is seen at 2.75% after a December hike, with risk of a move to 3%.

France is a defining 2027 risk with growth of 0.5% and a 5.2% deficit. DB assumes OAT premia stay elevated into the April/May election, then partly dissipate, and sees France as relatively attractive in rates and credit by mid-year.
UK growth is seen at 1.3% in 2027 after a surprise 1.6% in 2026. DB expects one more BoE hike to 4.25% in February, well below the 4.8% peak priced by markets, with CPI peaking just over 4%.
Japan: BoJ hikes of 25bp in December and March take the rate to 1.75%. An April 2027 consumption tax cut temporarily pushes inflation to 1.6%. USD/JPY is seen in the 140s.
China growth is forecast at 4.5% in 2027 with PBoC on hold at 1.25%. RMB is seen at 6.30 per dollar by end-2027, and the fiscal deficit widens to about 8% of GDP.
India: DB expects 7.2% growth, CPI at 5.3%, and repo hikes of 100bp in total to 6.25% by mid-2027. INR is seen at 98.50 per dollar by end-2027, and gold-loan NPAs are flagged as a risk.

Rates strategists are neutral on duration after being bearish, and expect steeper curves. They see 10y UST at 5.05% and Bund at 3.45% at end-2027, with short-term risks skewed lower and structural risks higher. Japan and France are the relative-value picks.

FX: DB raises its dollar forecast to a 'higher for longer' path. EUR/USD falls to 1.08 in H1 before recovering to 1.15 by end-2027. The USD's dependence on the AI capex boom is the main vulnerability.
Credit is moderately cautious. DB sees spreads risking an overshoot in Q1, with $IG up to 125bp and $HY up to 440bp. Fair-value 1H27 targets are $IG 95bp, $HY 345bp, €IG 115bp and €HY 395bp.
Credit top trades: hedge an AI capex slowdown with equity puts, underweight chipmakers, neoclouds and data centres, stay cautious on single-B US HY, and start neutral France.

Equity strategy: 2027 S&P EPS is forecast at $430 (+19%), and prices sit about 20% below levels implied by year-end earnings. Positioning is said to price only about 1% earnings growth. Overweight tech, financials, industrials, and metals and mining, with underweight in defensives.

Regional equity stance is tactically overweight US and Asia, underweight Europe, LatAm and EMEA. DB says Tech has been underperforming (-20pp) since the October downgrade, but is now long as the rotation has overshot.

Oil: Brent is forecast to average $90 in Q1 2027, $80 in Q2 and $70 in H2, with WTI near $67. Global inventories rose 52 mmbbl in October, implying 1.7 mmb/d oversupply. Iran and Hormuz remain the main risk.

EM: core rates volatility did most of the damage to EM in 2026. Growth FX is expected to take over from carry FX, with more cautious views on CEEMEA and LatAm carry. Policy credibility will separate winners.

Geopolitics: US pressure for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire is likely to rise in 2027. US-China competition broadens across chips, rare earths, robotics and drones, and the Busan trade truce expires on 10 Jan 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is far below earnings growth and the rotation away from tech has overshot.
Cyclical growth matters more than the rates curve.
Secular and cyclical tailwinds are intact.
Potential extra boost if a dollar downcycle begins.
Downside risks are rising after benefiting from war disruption.
Structural challenges, a cyclical upturn away from them, and unlikely sustained rate relief.
Healthcare is showing a turnaround and the REITs have idiosyncratic growth stories.
High yields threaten HY-rated AI ecosystem names and there is AI capex slowdown risk.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 EPS growth was 25% in Q1 2026, 34% in Q2 and 34% in Q3 (as stated by DB, already reported). DB forecasts 2027 S&P 500 EPS of $430 (+19%) and about 19% growth.
S&P 500 earnings level is about 20% above its 100-year trend channel. Growth outside tech, chips and memory is about 12%, and median company growth is about 15%.

Hyperscaler earnings slowed to the bottom of their long-run trend channel while hyperscaler capex growth is seen peaking. Hyperscalers have cut buybacks to finance capex but overall buybacks are at a new high.
DB forecasts global hyperscaler IG issuance of $280-320bn in 2027 vs $320bn in 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Resilient global growth with divergence underneath.
Modest slowdown as AI capex growth decelerates.
Sticky inflation supports further Fed tightening.
DB expects 25bp hikes in December, January and March.
Stable labour market with a low breakeven payroll.
Energy shock keeps inflation elevated until spring 2028.
DB is more dovish than market pricing.
CPI to peak just over 4% in early 2027.
Breaches RBI 6% tolerance, supporting rate hikes.
Oil relief baseline, highly geopolitically contingent.
Supports bond supply and term premium.

trade_ideas.description: Buy equity put options on S&P 500 and Eurostoxx 600 as a hedge against an AI capex slowdown
trade_ideas.rationale: Both indices screen expensive and AI capex is a key vulnerability.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight chipmakers, neoclouds and data centres in credit, and be very cautious on single-B US HY
trade_ideas.rationale: High yields threaten the HY-rated AI ecosystem and B spreads are tight.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically overweight Tech, US and EM Asia equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Rotation away from tech overshot and positioning is far below earnings growth.

risk_factors: AI capex overinvestment or a collapse in AI enthusiasm would hit growth, financial conditions and the USD.
French political and fiscal risk, including failure to agree a 2027 Budget or a Le Pen versus Mélenchon runoff.
Oil and geopolitical shocks, including Hormuz disruption or re-escalation with Iran.
Fiscal deficits and bond supply keeping term premia elevated.
Fed policy path uncertainty, with more tightening needed if inflation or wages firm.
Spreads could overshoot to $IG 125bp and $HY 440bp in Q1 2027 on an AI supply-chain slowdown.
vol_and_positioning: Equity strategists see last week's sell-off as a vol event that could go further. Positioning is moderately underweight large-cap equities and prices only about 1% earnings growth.
Core rates volatility in late Q3 and early Q4 hurt EM, and the Fed is retreating from forward guidance.
Credit team recommends equity put options as a short-term hedge against an AI capex slowdown, since S&P 500 and Eurostoxx 600 screen expensive.
Rates strategists argue AI and tokenisation could reduce short-term volatility but raise tail risks.
geopolitical: Middle East: US-Iran war is unresolved. Iran retains leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, and a temporary de-escalation mechanism looks more achievable than a full settlement.
Russia-Ukraine: US pressure for a ceasefire likely intensifies in 2027. A ceasefire would affect defence spending, sanctions and energy markets.

US-China: New export controls and tariffs are expected. Dated items include US polysilicon measures on 4 Dec 2026, defence-procurement restrictions on 1 Jan 2027, and higher Section 301 chip tariffs on 23 Jun. The Busan trade truce expires 10 Jan 2027.
European election supercycle: France presidential election on 18 Apr and 2 May, plus Spain, Italy, Finland, Greece, Slovakia and Poland.
US politics: Democratic midterm gains, the government funding deadline of 11 December, and a possible debt ceiling issue in late Q3 or early Q4 2027.
cross_bank_references: DB notes its view that US neutral has risen is 'now largely accepted' and still above the median Fed estimate of 3.2%.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth of 34% in Q2 and Q3 and prices about 20% below earnings-implied levels. Positioning prices only about 1% earnings growth, and buybacks are at a record.
tension_points.bear_case: The same AI cycle creates overinvestment risk. Credit strategists see equities as expensive and recommend put hedges, with spread risk to 125bp for $IG.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful downgrade to AI capex expectations or hyperscaler capex slowing abruptly.

tension_points.bull_case: Market pricing already compensates for political risk, banking is robust, and the RN is moving toward fiscal orthodoxy, so premia may dissipate after the election.
tension_points.bear_case: Failure to agree a 2027 Budget or a Le Pen versus Mélenchon runoff could produce much larger market costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No 2027 budget agreed, or Le Pen's lead narrowing so that a far-left candidate's odds rise.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings strength and demand-supply flows point to the S&P 500 at 9,000 by end-2027 despite the recent sell-off.
theme_stances.evidence: equity prices are around 20% below the levels implied by year-end 2027 earnings

theme_stances.key_argument: AI boom has lifted US real rates and equity inflows, supporting USD into H1 2027.
Above-target inflation and a higher neutral rate warrant 75bp more tightening.
